pit-crew.flag-yellow-local.comment: A local yellow is shown for an incident ahead — one short warning to slow down and mind the stopped cars. A full-course yellow takes the flag-yellow-full line instead.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-local.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow (local). In-sim: drive up to a stopped or spun car in a local yellow sector.

pit-crew.flag-yellow-full.comment: A full-course yellow is out — tells the driver the pace car is being deployed and to close up safely.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-full.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow (full). In-sim: a full-course caution in an oval race (the pace car is deployed).

pit-crew.flag-yellow-cleared.comment: A LOCAL yellow has been withdrawn — a short all-clear, replayed after a busier line finishes rather than dropped. It is spoken only for an episode that stayed local, because a local yellow ends with no flag shown at all and this line is the only way the driver learns the sector is clear. A full-course caution ends with a restart instead, and the restart is already announced — measured on an oval, it plays the start lights' go line — so no all-clear lands on top of it.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-cleared.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow Cleared plays the line on its own. In-sim: clear a local yellow sector. The other half of this line is the SILENCE after a caution — Harness → Flags → Caution → restart replays a full-course caution and restart captured at an oval through the translator; with the race session and hot-lap presets applied it must play the caution-waving, full-course yellow and green-held lines and then "Go, go, go!", with no all-clear behind them.

pit-crew.flag-green.comment: The green flag, when iRacing shows it without its start signal — as at the start of a practice or qualifying session. A race start, and a caution restart measured on an oval, carry that signal and play the start lights' go line instead. The wording differs per session type (practice, qualifying, race), so it branches on session.type; an unknown session type takes the race line.
pit-crew.flag-green.test: Harness → Flags → Green, after choosing a session preset (practice, qualifying or race). In-sim: the green at the start of a practice or qualifying session. Not at a race start, nor at a caution restart on an oval — both play "Go, go, go!" instead.

pit-crew.flag-blue.comment: A faster car is about to lap the driver — asks for mirrors and a clean pass.
pit-crew.flag-blue.test: Harness → Flags → Blue. In-sim: get shown the blue flag as a lapping car closes in.

pit-crew.flag-white.comment: The white flag — the leader's final lap in a race, or the last lap of a practice or qualifying session; the wording follows session.type, and an unknown session type takes the race line.
pit-crew.flag-white.test: Harness → Flags → White, after choosing a session preset. In-sim: the white flag comes out on the leader's final lap (race) or on your own last lap (practice, qualifying).

pit-crew.flag-white-last-lap.comment: The driver has crossed the line under the white flag and started their own last lap — give it everything. Race-only; stage two of the white-flag call.
pit-crew.flag-white-last-lap.test: Harness → Flags → White — Last Lap Started, with the race session preset. In-sim: cross start/finish while the white flag flies in a race.

pit-crew.flag-white-leader.comment: The overall leader has started their final lap while the driver is still some way behind — a heads-up that the race is about to end.
pit-crew.flag-white-leader.test: Harness → Flags → Leader's final lap, with the race session preset. In-sim: in a race, let the leader take the white flag while you are a lap or more down.

pit-crew.flag-red.comment: The red flag — the session is stopped; tells the driver to slow down and drive carefully back to the pits.
pit-crew.flag-red.test: Harness → Flags → Red. In-sim: a red flag in a hosted or league session.

pit-crew.flag-black.comment: A black flag has been issued — the driver has a penalty to serve within three laps.
pit-crew.flag-black.test: Harness → Flags → Black. In-sim: speed in the pit lane, or ignore a furled black flag; a race admin can also issue one (!black).

pit-crew.flag-checkered.comment: The checkered flag — the session is over. The wording follows session.type (the well-done only after a race); an unknown session type takes the race line.
pit-crew.flag-checkered.test: Harness → Flags → Checkered, after choosing a session preset. In-sim: take the checkered flag at the end of any session.

pit-crew.flag-debris.comment: A debris flag — something is on the track ahead; asks the driver to be careful.
pit-crew.flag-debris.test: Harness → Flags → Debris. In-sim: the debris flag after an incident leaves parts on the track.

pit-crew.flag-meatball.comment: The meatball flag — mandatory repairs, the driver must pit. Cuts any other line in flight and is never dropped.
pit-crew.flag-meatball.test: Harness → Flags → Meatball. In-sim: take enough damage that iRacing orders you in for repairs.

pit-crew.flag-disqualify.comment: The driver has been disqualified — pull off the track.
pit-crew.flag-disqualify.test: Harness → Flags → Disqualify. In-sim: exceed the session's incident limit, or a race admin disqualifies you (!dq).

pit-crew.flag-furled.comment: The furled black flag — the driver gained time and must give it back.
pit-crew.flag-furled.test: Harness → Flags → Furled. In-sim: cut a corner and gain time; the furled flag shows until the time is given back.

pit-crew.flag-furled-cleared.comment: The furled warning has been withdrawn after the driver gave the time back.
pit-crew.flag-furled-cleared.test: Harness → Flags → Furled, then Harness → Flags → Furled Cleared. In-sim: give the time back after a furled black flag.

pit-crew.flag-dq-scoring-invalid.comment: The driver has been disqualified and their scoring invalidated — DQ, scoring's off.
pit-crew.flag-dq-scoring-invalid.test: Harness → Flags → DQ — Scoring Invalid. In-sim: a disqualification that also invalidates scoring (rare; the harness is the practical route).

pit-crew.flag-crossed.comment: Crossed flags — the halfway point of the race. Race-only, while the driver is live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-crossed.test: Harness → Flags → Crossed, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: reach the halfway point of an oval race.

pit-crew.flag-one-pace-lap-to-go.comment: One more pace lap before the green on a rolling start — keep the spacing tidy and warm the tires. Race-only, live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-one-pace-lap-to-go.test: Harness → Flags → One Pace Lap to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: the second-to-last pace lap of a rolling start.

pit-crew.flag-green-held.comment: The pace car is pulling in and the green is imminent — get ready to launch. Rolling starts and restarts only; a standing-start grid is the start lights' business.
pit-crew.flag-green-held.test: Harness → Flags → Green Held, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: the final pace lap of a rolling start or restart, once the pace car peels off.

pit-crew.flag-ten-to-go.comment: Ten laps to go. Race-only, live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-ten-to-go.test: Harness → Flags → Ten to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: ten laps remaining in an oval race.

pit-crew.flag-five-to-go.comment: Five laps to go. Race-only, live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-five-to-go.test: Harness → Flags → Five to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: five laps remaining in an oval race.

pit-crew.flag-yellow-waving.comment: A waving yellow — a fresh incident right ahead, more urgent than the standing yellow. Repeats at most once per 30 seconds while the incident persists.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-waving.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow Waving. In-sim: approach a sector where a car has just crashed or spun.

pit-crew.flag-caution-waving.comment: The caution is out and waving — slow down and close up safely. Repeats at most once per 30 seconds.
pit-crew.flag-caution-waving.test: Harness → Flags → Caution Waving. In-sim: the caution comes out on an oval as the field bunches up.

pit-crew.pit-readback-entry.comment: Reads back the queued pit service as the car enters the pit lane, and again — without the opener — after the driver changes the queue while still on pit road. A limiter reminder leads on the initial entry when the car has one and it is off; nothing queued collapses the whole recap to the empty-fallback line.
pit-crew.pit-readback-entry.test: Harness → Pit Service Readback → Fire Readback, with Reason set to entry (entry-refire for the mid-lane replay) after setting a service snapshot with the Fuel Queued, Tires LF/RF/LR/RR (or the All / Fronts / Rears / Lefts / Rights / None presets), Compound, Fast Repair Queued / Available and Windshield Queued controls; leave Limiter Engaged unchecked for the pre-opener, and set damage on the Engine Warnings panel for the fast-repair slot. In-sim: queue fuel and two tires, then enter the pit lane.

pit-crew.pit-readback-exit.comment: Confirms the queued pit service a few seconds after the car leaves the pit lane — the same recap under a "to confirm" opener, which stays even when nothing is queued so the empty-fallback line still reads as a confirmation.
pit-crew.pit-readback-exit.test: Harness → Pit Service Readback → Fire Readback, with Reason set to exit after setting a service snapshot with the same controls. In-sim: queue a service, drive through the pits and out; the confirmation follows the pit-lane exit.

pit-crew.pit-window-opened.comment: Pit road has opened for the driver — one line, above ordinary chatter but below a flag, replayed after a busier line finishes rather than dropped because the window matters to strategy.
pit-crew.pit-window-opened.test: Harness → Pit Window → Pits opened. In-sim: the pits open in a race — after the field takes the green, or when a caution's pit window opens.

pit-crew.pit-window-closed.comment: Pit road has closed for the driver — the counterpart line. A rapid open/closed flurry replaces the stale in-flight line rather than stacking both.
pit-crew.pit-window-closed.test: Harness → Pit Window → Pits closed. In-sim: the pits close in a race — when the caution comes out on an oval, or in the final laps.

pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-most.comment: The track has gone from dry to mostly dry — the first hint of moisture, worth a heads-up before grip goes. Only the worsening direction takes this line; a rapid further step replaces it mid-sentence.
pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-most.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Mostly Dry. In-sim: rain starts falling on a dry track in a dynamic-weather session.

pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-very.comment: The track is now very lightly wet and getting wetter — a damp surface with real grip still available.
pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-very.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Very Lightly Wet. In-sim: light rain keeps falling on a mostly dry track.

pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-ligh.comment: The track is now lightly wet and getting wetter — the point where wet tires start to be a question.
pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-ligh.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Lightly Wet. In-sim: steady rain on a very lightly wet track.

pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-mode.comment: The track is now moderately wet and getting wetter — standing water is forming and the racing line is losing its grip.
pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-mode.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Moderately Wet. In-sim: heavier rain on a lightly wet track.

pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-very.comment: The track is now very wet and getting wetter — aquaplaning territory, a warning to back off.
pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-very.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Very Wet. In-sim: heavy rain on a moderately wet track.

pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-extr.comment: The track is now extremely wet — the wettest state the sim reports, and the most urgent of the worsening lines.
pit-crew.track-conditions-worsening-extr.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Extremely Wet. In-sim: a downpour on a very wet track.

pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-dry.comment: The track is fully dry again — the end of a drying trend, and the driest state the sim reports. Only the drying direction takes this line.
pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-dry.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Dry. In-sim: a mostly dry track finishes drying.

pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-mostly-.comment: The track has dried back to mostly dry — damp patches off the line, dry grip on it.
pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-mostly-.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Mostly Dry. In-sim: a very lightly wet track keeps drying.

pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-very-li.comment: The track has dried back to very lightly wet — nearly there, a dry line is forming.
pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-very-li.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Very Lightly Wet. In-sim: a lightly wet track keeps drying.

pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-lightly.comment: The track has dried back to lightly wet — the crossover window where slicks come back into the conversation.
pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-lightly.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Lightly Wet. In-sim: a moderately wet track keeps drying.

pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-moderat.comment: The track has dried back to moderately wet — standing water is draining and a line is starting to appear.
pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-moderat.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Moderately Wet. In-sim: a very wet track drying after the rain stops.

pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-very-we.comment: The track has dried back to very wet from extremely wet — the first step of a drying trend.
pit-crew.track-conditions-drying-very-we.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Very Wet. In-sim: the rain eases on an extremely wet track.

pit-crew.pit-box-five.comment: The pit-box count-in, 120 m out — the first of six marks spoken about a second apart on the approach to the driver's own box. Terse by design: the engine puts no radio frame around any mark, and a mark that cannot take the bus is dropped rather than replayed late.
pit-crew.pit-box-five.test: Harness → Pit Box → Five (120 m). In-sim: drive down pit road toward your own stall; the marks fire at 120, 100, 80, 60, 40 and 20 m.

pit-crew.pit-box-four.comment: The count-in's second mark, 100 m out.
pit-crew.pit-box-four.test: Harness → Pit Box → Four (100 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 100 m from the stall.

pit-crew.pit-box-three.comment: The count-in's third mark, 80 m out.
pit-crew.pit-box-three.test: Harness → Pit Box → Three (80 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 80 m from the stall.

pit-crew.pit-box-two.comment: The count-in's fourth mark, 60 m out.
pit-crew.pit-box-two.test: Harness → Pit Box → Two (60 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 60 m from the stall.

pit-crew.pit-box-one.comment: The count-in's fifth mark, 40 m out.
pit-crew.pit-box-one.test: Harness → Pit Box → One (40 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 40 m from the stall.

pit-crew.pit-box-pit-now.comment: The last mark, 20 m out — the cue to stop in the box.
pit-crew.pit-box-pit-now.test: Harness → Pit Box → Pit now (20 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 20 m from the stall.

pit-crew.corner-name-approaching.comment: The upcoming corner's bare name, spoken about a second before it in practice and test sessions — one clip, no radio frame, because at that lead the beeps would eat the whole margin. The name is the whole callout: a corner the voice has no clip for is skipped rather than half-said, and a pack that wants a lead-in puts it before the name here.
pit-crew.corner-name-approaching.test: Harness → Corner Names → Eau Rouge (or Turn 5). In-sim: a practice session on a track with corner data, Corner names enabled; the name plays on the approach to each corner.

pit-crew.damage-repair-needed.comment: The car has picked up damage the crew can repair — spoken once when iRacing first flags a mandatory or optional repair. A meatball flag carries the same news with more authority and outranks this line.
pit-crew.damage-repair-needed.test: Harness → Damage → Damage Detected. In-sim: hit a wall or another car hard enough for the repair indicator to light in the black box.

pit-crew.opponent-pit-leader.comment: The race leader has entered the pits — strategic news, spoken as one line. Every opponent-pit line queues behind a busier one rather than cutting it, because each describes a different car.
pit-crew.opponent-pit-leader.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Leader pitting. In-sim: a race where the leader pits while you are on track.

pit-crew.opponent-pit-ahead.comment: The car directly ahead in the standings has entered the pits.
pit-crew.opponent-pit-ahead.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Car ahead pitting. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you pits during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-pit-behind.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has entered the pits.
pit-crew.opponent-pit-behind.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Car behind pitting. In-sim: the car one place behind you pits during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-pit-nearby.comment: A car within two places of the driver has entered the pits, named by its position: the car-in lead-in, the number, the is-pitting tail. The number is read live at speak time and is part of the sentence — a position the voice cannot say skips the whole line, never the middle of it.
pit-crew.opponent-pit-nearby.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → P7 pitting (±2). In-sim: a car two places ahead or behind you pits during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-pit-others.comment: Several cars pitted in the same burst — the aggregate tail after the individual lines, so a pit train is not narrated car by car.
pit-crew.opponent-pit-others.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Several cars pitting. In-sim: a pit window opens and a group of cars dives in together.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-10.comment: The tank is estimated to cover ten more laps — ordinary commentary, spoken once when the estimate first drops through ten. A fresher count replaces a stale one still playing.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-10.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 10 laps of fuel left. In-sim: run a stint until the laps-of-fuel estimate falls through ten.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-9.comment: Nine laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-9.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 9 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through nine.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-8.comment: Eight laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-8.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 8 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through eight.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-7.comment: Seven laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-7.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 7 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through seven.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-6.comment: Six laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-6.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 6 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through six.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-5.comment: Five laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-5.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 5 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through five.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-4.comment: Four laps of fuel left — the last of the ordinary-commentary counts before the warnings start.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-4.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 4 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through four.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-3.comment: Three laps of fuel left — a warning at the flags' weight, so it takes the bus from ordinary chatter and is replayed rather than dropped behind a flag.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-3.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 3 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through three.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-2.comment: Two laps of fuel left — the second warning, same weight as the flags.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-2.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 2 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through two.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-1.comment: One lap of fuel left — critical: it cuts whatever is playing, because the next crossing is the box call.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-1.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 1 lap of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through one.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-box.comment: The tank will not cover another full lap — box this lap for fuel. Critical and interrupting: nothing in flight is worth more than this instruction.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-box.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → Box this lap. In-sim: keep running until the estimate falls below one lap.

pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-race-covered.comment: Good news inside the last ten laps: the tank covers the rest of the race with a lap in hand. Spoken once per stint, at ordinary weight — good news never needs to cut anything.
pit-crew.fuel-laps-left-race-covered.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → Enough fuel to finish. In-sim: with ten or fewer laps to go in a race, carry more fuel than the remaining distance needs.

pit-crew.pit-status-in-progress.comment: The crew has started working on the car. One of eight pit-status lines, each spoken once when iRacing's pit-service status changes to it; a newer status replaces the one still playing.
pit-crew.pit-status-in-progress.test: Harness → Pit Status → In Progress. In-sim: stop in the box with a service queued; the line plays as the crew starts.

pit-crew.pit-status-complete.comment: The service is finished and the car is ready to leave the box.
pit-crew.pit-status-complete.test: Harness → Pit Status → Complete. In-sim: wait out the queued service in the box; the line plays as the crew finishes.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-left.comment: The car stopped too far left of the box for the crew to work — the first, full correction; the terse repeat nag takes over while the error persists.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-left.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Left. In-sim: stop in the pit lane left of your box marks.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-right.comment: The car stopped too far right of the box — the first, full correction.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-right.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Right. In-sim: stop in the pit lane right of your box marks.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-forward.comment: The car overshot the box — the first, full correction.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-forward.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Forward. In-sim: stop past your box marks.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-back.comment: The car stopped short of the box — the first, full correction.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-back.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Back. In-sim: stop before your box marks.

pit-crew.pit-status-bad-angle.comment: The car is parked at an angle the crew cannot work at — the first, full correction.
pit-crew.pit-status-bad-angle.test: Harness → Pit Status → Bad Angle. In-sim: stop in the box with the car turned across it.

pit-crew.pit-status-cant-fix-that.comment: The crew cannot repair the damage this stop — the car is done.
pit-crew.pit-status-cant-fix-that.test: Harness → Pit Status → Can't Fix That. In-sim: pit with damage beyond what a pit stop can repair.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-left-repeat.comment: The terse nag that repeats every couple of seconds while the car sits too far left after the full correction.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-left-repeat.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Left, after Too Far Left. In-sim: stop left of the box and stay put; the nag repeats about every two seconds.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-right-repeat.comment: The repeat nag for too far right, as for too far left.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-right-repeat.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Right, after Too Far Right. In-sim: stop right of the box and stay put.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-forward-repe.comment: The repeat nag for too far forward, as for too far left.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-forward-repe.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Forward, after Too Far Forward. In-sim: overshoot the box and stay put.

pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-back-repeat.comment: The repeat nag for too far back, as for too far left.
pit-crew.pit-status-too-far-back-repeat.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Back, after Too Far Back. In-sim: stop short of the box and stay put.

pit-crew.pit-status-bad-angle-repeat.comment: The repeat nag for a bad angle, as for too far left.
pit-crew.pit-status-bad-angle-repeat.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Bad Angle, after Bad Angle. In-sim: park across the box and stay put.

pit-crew.rolling-start-pace-car.comment: The pace car has started moving the field onto the formation lap of a rolling start — get up to pace and close the gap. Race-only and live in the car; one of five takes.
pit-crew.rolling-start-pace-car.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Rolling Start → Pace car moving, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: sit on the grid of a rolling-start race and wait for the pace car to pull away.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-furled-ahead.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has been shown a furled black flag, named by its position: the car-in lead-in (the opponent-pit family's clip, reused because the words are the same), the number, then the furled tail. The number is part of the sentence — a position the voice cannot say skips the whole line. Every opponent-flag line queues behind a busier one rather than cutting it, because each describes a different car.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-furled-ahead.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: furled. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you picks up a furled black flag during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-furled-behind.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has been shown a furled black flag.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-furled-behind.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: furled. In-sim: the car one place behind you picks up a furled black flag during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-furled-track-ahea.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track carries a furled black flag — a safety-weighted heads-up, since a penalised car may be slow.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-furled-track-ahea.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: furled. In-sim: close in on a car ahead on the road that has a furled black flag.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-black-ahead.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has been black-flagged, named by its position — car-in, the number, the black tail. The number is part of the sentence.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-black-ahead.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: black flag. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you is black-flagged during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-black-behind.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has been black-flagged — the pressure from behind should ease.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-black-behind.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: black flag. In-sim: the car one place behind you is black-flagged during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-black-track-ahead.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track has been black-flagged — a safety-weighted heads-up.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-black-track-ahead.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: black flag. In-sim: close in on a black-flagged car ahead on the road.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-meatball-ahead.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has the meatball (repair) flag, named by its position — car-in, the number, the meatball tail. The number is part of the sentence.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-meatball-ahead.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: meatball. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you is shown the meatball flag during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-meatball-behind.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has the meatball flag and will be coming in for repairs.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-meatball-behind.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: meatball. In-sim: the car one place behind you is shown the meatball flag during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-meatball-track-ah.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track has the meatball flag — a damaged car that could be slow, so a safety-weighted warning.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-meatball-track-ah.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: meatball. In-sim: close in on a car ahead on the road that is showing the meatball flag.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-disqualify-ahead.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has been disqualified, named by its position — car-in, the number, the disqualified tail. The number is part of the sentence.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-disqualify-ahead.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: DQ. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you is disqualified during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-disqualify-behind.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has been disqualified.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-disqualify-behind.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: DQ. In-sim: the car one place behind you is disqualified during a race.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-disqualify-track-.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track has been disqualified and may pull off — a safety-weighted heads-up.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-disqualify-track-.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: DQ. In-sim: close in on a disqualified car ahead on the road.

pit-crew.opponent-flag-others.comment: Several cars around the driver picked up penalty flags in the same burst — the aggregate tail after the individual lines. It only ever describes flags the user opted into, because the per-flag opt-ins are applied before anything reaches the aggregate.
pit-crew.opponent-flag-others.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Several cars flagged. In-sim: a multi-car incident that hands penalties to several cars near you at once.

pit-crew.limiter-on-track.comment: The pit limiter is still on about a second and a half after the car left pit road — the driver forgot to switch it off.
pit-crew.limiter-on-track.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter on out on track (fires about 1.5 s later). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, leave pit road with the limiter still engaged.

pit-crew.limiter-missing.comment: The car is on pit road without its limiter engaged, a couple of seconds after the pit-entry reminder went unheeded — an escalation, not a duplicate.
pit-crew.limiter-missing.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter off on pit road (fires about 2.5 s later). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, enter pit road without engaging it and keep it off.

pit-crew.limiter-dropped.comment: The limiter was switched off while the car is still between the pit cones — turn it back on.
pit-crew.limiter-dropped.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter dropped. In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, disengage it while still on pit road.

pit-crew.limiter-speeding.comment: The car is over the pit speed limit on a car that has a limiter — the fix is to press the button, which is why this line is separate from the no-limiter one.
pit-crew.limiter-speeding.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Speeding (limiter car). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, exceed the pit speed limit on pit road.

pit-crew.start-light-ready.comment: The start gantry has lit — lights are up, the standing start is seconds away. Critical and interrupting, and replayed rather than lost if a spotter call holds the bus; a later go line replaces it if it never got out.
pit-crew.start-light-ready.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Ready, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: the red lights come on for a standing start.

pit-crew.start-light-go.comment: Go, go, go — the moment iRacing releases the field: lights out at a standing start, the green at a rolling start, and the green at a caution restart (measured on an oval). Critical and interrupting: it cuts anything in flight, including a ready line still playing.
pit-crew.start-light-go.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Go, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car); Harness → Flags → Caution → restart plays it at a restart. In-sim: the lights go out at a standing start, the field is released at a rolling start, or the green comes out at a caution restart on an oval.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-90.comment: Ninety seconds to the start — the first get-in-the-car reminder, spoken from the garage or session screen too. Ordinary weight, and dropped rather than replayed stale if the bus is busy.
pit-crew.start-light-countdown-90.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 90, with the race session preset. In-sim: sit in the garage as a standing-start race counts down.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-60.comment: Sixty seconds to the start — the same reminder, one mark closer.
pit-crew.start-light-countdown-60.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 60, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes sixty seconds.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-30.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 30, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes thirty seconds.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-10.comment: Ten seconds to the start — the last mark before the gantry lights.
pit-crew.start-light-countdown-10.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 10, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes ten seconds.

pit-crew.incident-off-track.comment: The driver ran off track — a short coaching line about track limits, with no point count (the type has none worth stating). A faster, worse incident in the same crash replaces this line mid-sentence.
pit-crew.incident-off-track.test: Harness → Incidents → Off Track (1x). In-sim: put four wheels off in any session.

pit-crew.incident-out-of-control.comment: The driver lost control of the car (a spin) — a calm-down line, no point count.
pit-crew.incident-out-of-control.test: Harness → Incidents → Out of Control (2x). In-sim: spin the car.

pit-crew.incident-contact-world.comment: Light contact with the wall or scenery: the type line, then the points it cost as a separate clause. The count is optional because it is a whole sentence of its own — a light touch worth no points, or a count the voice has no clip for, leaves the type line standing on its own.
pit-crew.incident-contact-world.test: Harness → Incidents → Contact — Wall (0x) (the type line alone) or Collision — Wall (2x) for a count. In-sim: brush a wall lightly.

pit-crew.incident-collision-world.comment: A hard hit on the wall or scenery: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause.
pit-crew.incident-collision-world.test: Harness → Incidents → Collision — Wall (2x). In-sim: hit a wall hard.

pit-crew.incident-contact-car.comment: Light contact with another car: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause — nothing when the rub cost none.
pit-crew.incident-contact-car.test: Harness → Incidents → Contact — Car (0x). In-sim: rub doors with another car.

pit-crew.incident-collision-car.comment: A heavy collision with another car: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause — four on pavement, two on dirt, whatever the sim scored, and nothing for a count the voice cannot say.
pit-crew.incident-collision-car.test: Harness → Incidents → Collision — Car (4x), Collision — Car (2x, dirt) or Collision — Car (escalated). In-sim: a hard collision with another car.

pit-crew.no-limiter-speeding.comment: Over the pit speed limit on a car that has NO pit limiter — the fix is to lift, so this line must never mention a limiter. The mirror of limiter-speeding; exactly one of the two speaks to any car.
pit-crew.no-limiter-speeding.test: Harness → No Pit Limiter → Speeding (no limiter). In-sim: on a car without a pit limiter, exceed the pit speed limit on pit road.

pit-crew.no-limiter-entry.comment: Pit entry on a car with no limiter: a reminder to mind the limit, then the limit itself — intro, number, unit — as one optional clause. The number is the whole point of the clause and a fragment of its sentence, so a limit the voice has no clip for drops the clause entirely rather than speaking the intro into silence; the reminder still stands alone as a complete sentence.
pit-crew.no-limiter-entry.test: Harness → No Pit Limiter → Pit entry reminder, after Harness → Session Start → Fire Session Start with the Pit speed limit set (the limit clause reads that snapshot; without one only the reminder plays). In-sim: on a car without a pit limiter, enter pit road.

pit-crew.lap-time-best.comment: A new session-best lap, or the driver's first valid lap: the intro (best-lap-yet or first-good-lap), then the time as minute, seconds and tenths. The minute is a hard if here — a terse pack may write it as optional, since the assumed minute is understood, but only where that minute is 1; every other component is required, because a time missing its seconds is not a time.
pit-crew.lap-time-best.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Lap Time → Best Lap 1:03.4 (Best Lap 0:34.8 for a lap without the minute, First Valid Lap 2:07.0 for the other intro). In-sim: set a personal best in any session, or complete the first clean lap of a session.

pit-crew.gap-trend.comment: The gap to a standings neighbor has turned: we are gaining on the car ahead, it is pulling away, the car behind is gaining, or we are dropping it. The line is chosen by side and direction; the live gap readout follows through the gap-readout fragment. Both gap lines share one cooldown (30 s by default), so a second one inside it stays silent.
pit-crew.gap-trend.test: Harness → Gaps → Trend: closing on car ahead, Trend: car ahead pulling away, Trend: car behind gaining or Trend: dropping the car behind — the seconds clause needs a live gap, so drive the harness session with cars around you. In-sim: race with a car a few seconds ahead and close on it lap after lap.

pit-crew.gap-threshold.comment: The gap to a standings neighbor first dropped under the driver's alert threshold — we have caught the car ahead, or the car behind is right with us — then the live gap through the same gap-readout fragment. Shares the trend line's cooldown.
pit-crew.gap-threshold.test: Harness → Gaps → Caught the car ahead (threshold) or Car behind within threshold, with a live gap for the seconds clause. In-sim: close to within the configured gap threshold of the car ahead.

pit-crew.race-status.comment: The every-three-laps status update while the driver holds position in a race: the leader hears the whole still-leading line (still leading our class in a multi-class race), everyone else hears "we're currently" and the live position. Both branches are read at speak time, so a deferred update is never stale. The number is part of the sentence and stays required.
pit-crew.race-status.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race → Status update (P5 on lap 7) or Leader status (P1 on lap 6) — both are MUTE in the harness, which has no live position for the readout to speak, so only the fire attempt shows in the log. In-sim: hold the same race position for three consecutive laps after the green; the update comes as you cross the line on the third.

pit-crew.toggle-fuel-on.comment: The driver queued fuel for the next stop — a short acknowledgment (got it / roger that / copy that) then the confirmation, the shape every toggle confirmation in this family shares. The acknowledgment is pit-actions/acknowledgment, a different pool from the generic acknowledgment/acknowledgment: a smaller set tuned for this register, with its own no-repeat tracker by virtue of being a different group and base, so no named pool is needed for the two to stay independent. Silent for a few seconds after leaving the pit lane, when the sim resets the queue on its own.
pit-crew.toggle-fuel-on.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fuel ON, not within about 4.5 s of Exited Pit Lane (the pit-action cooldown). In-sim: press the fuel toggle in the pit black box, or on a Fuel Service key.

pit-crew.toggle-fuel-off.comment: The driver removed fuel from the next stop — acknowledgment, then the confirmation.
pit-crew.toggle-fuel-off.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fuel OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the fuel toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-all.comment: All four tires queued — acknowledgment, then the confirmation. Each tire line answers the RESULTING set, whichever buttons got the driver there.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-all.test: Harness → Tire Service → All, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all four tires in the pit black box.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-fronts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Fronts, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the front tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rears.test: Harness → Tire Service → Rears, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the rear tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rights.test: Harness → Tire Service → Rights, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the right-side tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-lf.comment: The left-front only — a puncture-style single change.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rf.test: Harness → Tire Service → RF only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the right-front tire.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-lr.test: Harness → Tire Service → LR only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the left-rear tire.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rf-lr.test: Harness → Tire Service → RF + LR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the right-front and left-rear tires.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rr.comment: Three corners — everything but the right-rear.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rr.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except RR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the right-rear.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lr.comment: Three corners — everything but the left-rear.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lr.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except LR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the left-rear.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rf.comment: Three corners — everything but the right-front.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rf.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except RF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the right-front.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lf.comment: Three corners — everything but the left-front.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lf.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except LF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the left-front.

pit-crew.tire-set-off.comment: Every tire cleared from the next stop — spoken only when the resulting set is empty, never on a side-switch that merely removes some tires.
pit-crew.tire-set-off.test: Harness → Tire Service → Skip, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear every tire in the pit black box.

pit-crew.tire-compound-dry.comment: The compound for the next stop switched to dry. The one confirmation for the switch — the all-four-tires event iRacing raises alongside it is suppressed before it reaches the engineer.
pit-crew.tire-compound-dry.test: Harness → Tire Service → Compound → DRY, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch the pit-service compound to dry.

pit-crew.tire-compound-wet.comment: The compound for the next stop switched to wet.
pit-crew.tire-compound-wet.test: Harness → Tire Service → Compound → WET, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch the pit-service compound to wet.

pit-crew.toggle-windshield-on.comment: A windshield clean queued for the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-windshield-on.test: Harness → Pit Service → Windshield ON, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: press the windshield toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.toggle-windshield-off.test: Harness → Pit Service → Windshield OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the windshield toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-on.comment: A fast repair queued for the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-on.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fast Repair ON, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: press the fast-repair toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-off.comment: The fast repair removed from the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-off.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fast Repair OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the fast-repair toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.overtake-gained-position.comment: The position readout after a gained overtake — "We're currently", then the live position — played once the reaction line has finished. It is skipped for a podium gain, whose reaction line already states the place, and never doubles a position announced by another line in the last 20 seconds. The lead-in is an optional clause: a second readout within 30 seconds that moved at most one place says the bare number ("P four"), which is a complete, true statement on its own; a script that always wants the lead-in drops the optional.
pit-crew.overtake-gained-position.test: Harness: mute — the Overtakes buttons fire the reaction but the harness has no live position, so this readout has nothing to say there. In-sim: pass a car in a race outside the top three; the reaction (when it rolls) is followed by the current position, and a second pass within half a minute reads the bare number.

pit-crew.overtake-lost-position.comment: The position readout after a lost place — the same lead-in and live number as the gained readout, under the same 20-second no-double rule and the same optional lead-in.
pit-crew.overtake-lost-position.test: Harness: mute — the Overtakes → Lost — now P5 button fires the reaction but the harness has no live position for this readout. In-sim: get passed in a race; the come-on line (when it rolls) is followed by the current position.

pit-crew.race-end.comment: The final result as the driver crosses the line after the checkered: the driver's name, then one line per result — we won, second place, the podium in third, or the race-is-over line with the position number for fourth or worse. The greeting is optional because names are a union across voices and the result reads whole without it; the position number is part of the last line and stays required. Deferred behind a same-lap best-lap readout rather than cutting it — the race is over either way.
pit-crew.race-end.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race → Race over — P1 (we won!), or Race over — P2 (second place), Race over — P3 (podium) and Race over — P9 (mid-pack) for the other branches, Race over — multi-class P15 / class P1 for a class win. In-sim: take the checkered flag in a race and cross the line.

pit-crew.position-change.comment: The driver's position after a completed lap, in one of three shapes: an invalidated qualifying lap says "That lap didn't count", then "We're currently" and the position; a lap that put the driver on pole says the pole line alone; every other lap says the intro ("That puts us to" for a gain in qualifying, "We're currently" otherwise, and always in a race) and the position, read live in a race. Practice stays silent, and a race hold is left to the race-status update.
pit-crew.position-change.test: Harness → Position → Improved 5 → 3, Worsened 3 → 5, First Valid Lap P1, Qualifying P1 (pole), Holding P1 (qualifying, slow lap), Unchanged P5 (non-PB lap) or the Invalid lap, … buttons (all qualifying). The race branch is mute in the harness (no live position) — In-sim: complete a race lap having gained or lost a place.

pit-crew.overtake-gained.comment: The reaction to a gained overtake, one line chosen by what the pass earned: the lead (overall, or in class in a multi-class race), second or third place — each of those states the position itself, so no readout follows — or the plain "Nice pass" for anything else, which the separate position readout then completes. A podium pass always reacts; any other pass reacts about one time in three, and a place gained because a car ahead retired never does.
pit-crew.overtake-gained.test: Harness → Overtakes → Gained — now P5 (nice pass), Gained the lead (P2 → P1), Gained — multi-class (class P3 → P2), Gained — P3 → P2 (podium line), Gained — P4 → P3 (podium line); Gained — retirement (readout only) stays silent here. In-sim: pass a car cleanly in a race.

pit-crew.overtake-lost.comment: The reaction to a lost place: "Come on, <name>." in the driver's chosen name, then "Don't give up positions like that." The opener is a complete sentence of its own and is optional — a voice without a clip for the chosen name skips it and the line still plays. A lost podium place always reacts; any other loss about one time in three.
pit-crew.overtake-lost.test: Harness → Overtakes → Lost — now P5. In-sim: get passed in a race.

pit-crew.qualifying-invalidation-lap-inv.comment: An incident on a counted qualifying lap: the invalidated line always, then — only in lap-limited qualifying, where a count means something — a tail for how many counted laps remain: out of laps, one to five by count (each a whole sentence with its own encouragement), or plenty above five. The tail is a whole clause, so an if with no else is right for it; a count the case has no key for says nothing. One callout per lap however many incidents; silent on out-laps and beyond the counted attempts.
pit-crew.qualifying-invalidation-lap-inv.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Qualifying Invalidation → Off-Track — 3 laps left (Contact-Car — 1 lap left, Off-Track — out of laps, Off-Track — plenty of laps, Off-Track — time-limited for the other tails; the four (silent) buttons and Same Lap Again (latch) for the suppressions). In-sim: go off track on a flying lap of a lap-limited qualifying session.

pit-crew.race-start.comment: The grid brief a few seconds into a race session: the driver's name, the starting position (from pole, or qualifying put us to P N), the track and air temperatures, the track wetness, and a setup nudge when the loaded setup looks like a qualifying one. Every clause but the wetness is optional because each is a whole clause the brief reads true without — a name, a position number or a temperature the voice cannot say drops its own clause and nothing else; the position branch is a case inside its clause so a pack can rephrase pole and composed apart. The wetness intro and state are required: the brief always ends on the track.
pit-crew.race-start.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race Start → Race start — P5, with the race session preset (Race start — P1 (pole), Race start — P65 (out of range) and Race start — no position for the other position branches; the setup nudge has no harness route — In-sim: load a setup whose name matches the qualifying pattern under Setup Warning Patterns). In-sim: sit through the transition into a race session; the brief comes about three seconds in.

pit-crew.session-start.comment: The brief a few seconds into a practice or qualifying session (a race takes the race-start brief instead): the driver's name, which session it is, the pit speed limit with its unit, the track and air temperatures, the track wetness, and — in qualifying only — a setup nudge when the loaded setup looks like a race one. The greeting, the pit-speed limit, both temperatures and the nudge are optional because each is a whole clause the brief reads true without: a name, a limit or a temperature the voice cannot say drops its own clause and nothing else. The session line and the wetness are required — a brief that names no session, or stops at "and the track is", is not a brief.
pit-crew.session-start.test: Harness → Session Start → Fire Session Start, with Session type set to practice or qualifying (race is silent here — it is the race-start callout's); Fire as Fresh Connect covers the mid-session connect. The setup nudge has no harness route — In-sim: in qualifying, load a setup whose name matches the race pattern under Setup Warning Patterns. In-sim: join a practice or qualifying session; the brief comes about three seconds after the session begins, in the garage or on track.

pit-crew.spotter-call.comment: A spotter transition call — a car has appeared alongside, a second one joined it, one of two has gone, or the sides swapped: "Car left", "Two cars right", "Three wide", "Clear right, car left", with inside/outside terms on an oval. The spotter engine picks the clip for the exact transition and hands it over as the spotterClip var, so the call is that one step; it cuts anything in flight and is never replayed late. No radio frame: the beeps would drown a call that has to land at once.
pit-crew.spotter-call.test: Harness → Radar → Left, Right, Both Sides, Two Left, Two Right (each from the state the button names). In-sim: let a car pull alongside in any session with the spotter enabled.

pit-crew.spotter-info.comment: The spotter's informational lines — "Clear" once the car alongside has genuinely separated, and the still-there reminder ("Still there", "Hold your line") on its cadence while a car stays alongside. The same engine-picked spotterClip step as the call, at a lower weight so a reminder can never chop a critical line. No radio frame.
pit-crew.spotter-info.test: Harness → Radar → Clear (after Left or Right); the still-there reminder repeats on its own while a side stays occupied. In-sim: hold a car alongside for a few seconds, then let it go.

radio.comment: The walkie-talkie frame: an open tick, the pit-lane ambience bed, a close tick.

readback-body.comment: The service recap both readbacks share: fuel, tires or compound, a beat, then fast repair and windshield only when there is something to say. Each slot is a whole clause, so a slot that resolves to nothing leaves a shorter recap that is still true.

gap-readout.comment: The live gap readout both gap lines share: "Gap is", the whole seconds, the tenths. One optional clause, not three optional steps — the three vars resolve on a single check (the gap is readable, under a minute, and still to the car the line named), so the readout is spoken whole or left out whole, and the line before it is a complete sentence either way.
